properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/22/2025 to MINARD RUN OIL CO in Jenks Township, Forest county. CSL 307(a) - INDUSTRIAL WASTE DISCHARGES - Industrial waste discharged, directly or indirectly, into Waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit, authorization, or contrary to rules and regulations of the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: MINARD RUN OIL CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/22/2025
Violation Code: CSL 307(a) - INDUSTRIAL WASTE DISCHARGES - Industrial waste discharged, directly or indirectly, into Waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit, authorization, or contrary to rules and regulations of the Department.
Violation ID: 8259791
Permit API: 053-26767
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Jenks Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/22/2025
Comments: This inspection occurred in response to a phone call made by Dan McCamey, of Minard Run Oil Company (MROC) on December 22, 2025. The purpose of the phone call was to report an incident which had occurred at Warrant 5107 Well #25P (API# 053-26767). A failure in the buried steel pipeline leading to this well resulted in leaking crude oil rising to the surface. A well tender spotted the crude oil earlier today and notified MROC immediately. A work crew arrived soon thereafter to repair the line, install containment, and begin remediating the released crude oil. Upon my arrival to the site, the pipeline had been repaired which stopped the release. The released crude oil had migrated down the road ditch for approximately 20 feet, across the road through a culvert, flowing downhill into a spring, ultimately entering Guiton Run (HQ-CWF) at (41.513992, -79.18582) after traveling approximately 50 yards. Pockets of weathered crude oil and emulsion were evident downstream for approximately 475 yards ending at (41.512156, -79.189991). The amount of crude oil released as a result of this incident was unknown due to the lack of accumulated product at the site. At this time, it is estimated that less than one barrel of product was released. A siphon dam was installed in the road ditch, beyond the direction of flow where the crude oil was initially spotted. A second siphon dam was installed and lined beyond the road culvert. Booms and diapers were already placed on the surface and at the point of entry in Guiton Run. Booms and diapers should be regularly monitored and replaced as necessary until the site is deemed remediated. Additional booms and diapers should be placed in Guiton Run to absorb and capture any released crude oil within the stream. The stream should be continuously monitored until there is no longer any evidence of crude oil. Follow up inspections will routinely be conducted to monitor remediation of this release. Confirmatory field screening and/or sampling will need to be conducted to verfiy that the cleanup is deemed complete prior to any seeding/mulching. The Department's Policy 800-5000-001- "Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites or Access Roads" sets forth the procedure to be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release documented in this Notice of Violation ("NOV"), by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. The conventional well was equipped for production with a pump jack. The well name, API number, and operator information were displayed on a sign attached to the pump jack.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/23/2024 to STONEHAVEN ENERGY MGT CO LLC in Bloom Township, Clearfield county. 78.91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under 25 Pa. Code §§ 78.92—78.98 or an approved alternate method.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STONEHAVEN ENERGY MGT CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/23/2024
Violation Code: 78.91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under 25 Pa. Code §§ 78.92—78.98 or an approved alternate method.
Violation ID: 8202416
Permit API: 033-26543
Unconventional: No
County: Clearfield
Municipality: Bloom Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/23/2024
Comments: On 9/12/2024, the Department received a call regarding a bubbling hole located in the vicinity of the above-referenced gas well. On 9/17/2024, I investigated the area of concern and found a hole located along the right of way for power lines that was continuously bubbling. At that time, I confirmed that the bubbling was combustible gas with an Altair 5X gas meter (100% methane/volume). Additional investigation indicated that the suspected source of the bubbling was from a leaking pipeline that is believed to be associated with the Bickle #4 gas well. The location of the bubbling was marked with pink flagging at the following coordinates: 41.0275 / -78.651667. At the time of this inspection on 9/23/2024, the weather was 63¿¿ with rain. This inspection was conducted to follow-up on the 9/17/2024 investigation into the suspected leaking pipeline that is believed to be associated with the Bickle #4 gas well. There was one open annulus vent on the wellhead and 0% combustible gas was detected at the time of inspection. Two small leaks (10% methane/volume) were detected at the fitting connecting the line to the drip and on the housing seam of the secondary meter. The violations referenced above are continuing violations. Stonehaven will be contacted to address the bubbling along the right of way and the leaks at the fittings that were identified during this inspection. No new violations cited at this time. The requested written response should include what measures have been or need to be taken to fix the leak on the pipeline associated with this well by 10/04/2024

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 07/30/2020 to DL RESOURCES INC in Oakland Twp, Butler county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DL RESOURCES INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 07/30/2020
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 890283
Permit API: 019-21522
Unconventional: Yes
County: Butler
Municipality: Oakland Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 07/30/2020
Comments: This inspection has been conducted in response to an anonymous complaint submitted to the Department on July 29, 2020. The complaint alleged that a poly brine tank, associated with Well #: 019-21522(Haugh 1), was damaged, and has been leaking brine on to the ground surface for some time. These allegations have been verified in the field. A large crack exists on the eastern facing side of the tank. Fluid seems to have drained at a slow but steady rate from above the crack. It is unclear how much fluid has drained from the tank over time. An earthen containment exits around the tank. The leaked fluid, however, seems to be traveling directly down through the soil. It is not clear as to where the fluid is migrating to beyond the contained area. There are no clear outlets in the area immediately beyond the containment. It is recommended that the tank be repaired or replaced to comply with regulatory requirements associated with petroleum brine management and storage.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78.122(A) - WELL REPORTING – WELL RECORD – Operator failed to keep a detailed drillers log at well site or submit a complete well record, on a form provided by the Department, within 30 days of cessation of drilling or altering.
Violation ID: 8154324
Permit API: 121-45433
Unconventional: No
County: Venango
Municipality: Sugarcreek Borough
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/03/2023
Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023 and a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3589928 dated 7/21/2023. Onsite with DEP staff Alicia Furey and Lucas Eichner to collect a water sample from the earthen dike. The earthen dike is retaining fluid inside the bottom of the entire dike. There is approximately 4-5" of oily water pooled inside the dike. The dike drain remains closed and plugged. Water flowing into a separator barrel on top of a steel oil tank could be heard from the ground.Prior to the site visit water samples of the Bellows Spring was collected for analysis. There are 4 separate pipes flowing water into the cistern for the spring. Each pipe was identified, labeled, and sampled separately.After collecting samples from the earthen dike, DEP staff walked the hillside between the tank battery and Bellows Spring. The goal was to investigate any other oil and gas activity that may be located above the spring and that would be a potential contributor to the impact of the Bellows Spring. There was nothing observed between the tank battery and the Bellows Spring relating to oil and gas activity.At 2:05pm Mr. Rhoades was called via phone by the Department. The current condition of the tank battery was discussed with Mr. Rhoades and he indicated that a water truck is scheduled for next week to empty the dike and the brine tanks. Mr. Rhoades also stated that he has hired Moody and Associates as a consultant and that a check was in the mail to obtain their services. The Department clearly communicated the importance and urgency of starting the cleanup process at the site including the earthen dike area. Mr. Rhoades seemed to understand and asked if the water was good to drink yet in Reno and if individual households are being tested. I explained to Mr. Rhoades that samples have been taken from the spring by Oil and Gas Operations and that I was unaware of any other sampling/testing. It was also stated that the "Do not Consume" advisory has not yet been lifted from my knowledge at the time. The phone call was concluded with Mr. Rhoades indicating that he is starting the process to clean things up.

Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/04/2026
Comments: On 2/4/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 10 degrees and mostly clear when I arrived on location. Due to frozen conditions, conductivity readings were not taken during this inspection.When I arrived at the active north pad, I met with Seneca's Mark McCormick who described current operations as follows. Drilling to total depth has been completed on eight new gas wells at the site. Crews were on site, prepping for upcoming stimulation operations on the eight wells. Frac equipment was being mobilized to the location. Fracking has not commenced but is expected to start on 2/12/2026 depending on when the crew finishes on the DCNR 007 L Pad and depending on weather. Mark expects stimulation activities on the eight wells to be completed by the end of June 2026. In addition to 28 frac tanks that were stationed on the west side of the pad during previous operations, four pump down frac tanks, two gas buster frac tanks and five working frac tanks have been staged on the pad. Five wells have been completed at the site and were staged for production. Three sand separators remain near the wells but have been disconnected.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water/ice. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. The original south pad and access road for the Taft 851 1V well have been returned to original grade.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations.The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 0930 hours.

The wellhead is in fairly close, but not visible proximity to the production facility (photo #2). At the wellhead the surface casing valve is open, lower right side production tubular valve closed to port, lower production tubular left side valve is open, upper production tubular is plumbed with no valve unions, left side of head plumbed tubular to sales/surface equipment has open valve; annulus is buried, unable to determine if vented (photo #3). Well label/marker is affixed to wellhead on lubricator (photo #5). The wellhead is in fairly close, but not visible proximity to the production facility and requires a well label/marker (photos #2 and #5). Some trace to occasionally moderate corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, and tubulars. The surface/ground production facility and one 50 bbl poly tank all contained by a shallow earthen dike (photo #6). Valve closed on main tubular feeding facility but open valves to and from separator (photo #7). A 31-day production chart is present, with cycling markings dated 9/2/22 (photo #8). No Well posting signage is affixed anywhere at facility. Notice of Violation issued on 12/12/2019 for Well posting OGA3211(G) continues and is outstanding. The Department is requesting Operator add contact address information to the permanent well posting signage affixed at the surface production facility. The Operator has not submitted 2021 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well. No MIA submitted by the Operator for 2021, 2020, and 2019. The last MIA value officially submitted was back in 2018 stating 55 psig. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Operating Wells - Mechanical Integrity reporting 78.88(e). The Operator submitted annual production reported (APR) in 2021 of 0 Mcf recorded over 365 days. The 2021 annual production report submitted indicates that this well was not in production during the 2021 production year. Additionally, this well was noted as having 0 or blank production values under the gas and/or oil quantity columns and noted as Well Temporarily Not Producing under the non production comments columns of the 2021 and 2020 production reports. The last reported production value was in 2019 of 2,701 Mcf recorded over 365 days. This well appears to be back in production based on this inspection, the chart at facility with recordings, and the open valves at wellhead and separator.

Permit API: 123-47186
Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/27/2026
Comments: This conventional well is equipped to produce with a pump jack, a site ID sign is posted on the jack. There are no surface concerns evident on the well site at this time. 2025 APR and MIA information were submitted for this well.The tank battery for Trinity Mineral Partners' Roell lease is located approximately 500 feet to the west of this well, and is accessed off of Rounds Hill Road.This tank battery consists of two earthen containments. One containment consists of two 210 bbl stock tanks and separators, there are no surface issues evident at this containment. A second earthen containment (located southwest/downslope of the aforementioned one) holds a horizontal (approximate 250 bbl capacity) steel production water tank. There is an approximate 10' x 200' area that has been recently excavated beyond the end of the spur road that is used to access the tank battery, and continues adjacent to and downslope of, the production water tank/containment and ends at the edge of the bank that runs parallel to Rounds Hill Road. Mulch has been sparsely applied across the excavated area. Deer tracks are prevalent throughout the excavated area downslope of the production water tank/containment.Water is seeping out of the southwest corner of the production water tank containment, the specific conductance (SPC) of this water is elevated (> 1000 uS/cm). The SPC of the material at (and downslope of) the southwest corner of the production water tank containment is also elevated. Elevated SPC continues to be observed in standing water and the soil within the aforementioned excavated area downslope of the production water tank containment. Beyond the excavated area, there is an approximate 50 foot section of stressed vegetation evident on the bank of Rounds Hill Road. The SPC of the soil along this section of road bank is also elevated. The SPC of the Rounds Hill Road ditch water downslope of the aforementioned area of stressed vegetation is approximately ten times higher than the ditch water upslope of this point. The Rounds Hill Road ditch water continues to have elevated SPC for another 200 feet until the ditch enters an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Jackson Run.There was no obvious discharge from the production water tank during this inspection, the prevalence of elevated SPC and stressed vegetation in the material that comprises the containment and areas downslope of the containment is indicative of production water discharges into the containment due to poor housekeeping and/or a lack of tank integrity. The evidence obtained during this inspection also indicates that the containment surrounding the production water tank was not constructed in a manner to prevent the tank contents from reaching waters of this Commonwealth.An SAC 942 water sample was collected from standing water located in the excavated area downslope of the production water tank containment.In addition to the information requested in the attached Notice of Violation, it is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners reveal how the aforementioned excavated soil was disposed and provide any supporting documentation regarding its disposal.

Comments: Melissa Breitenbach (XTO) called the Department on August 11, 2026 to report a release at the Bachelder Well Pad. It was hypothesized that one of the tank valves had failed, resulting in a leak that mixed with precipitation in the containment walls. The walls on the eastern edge of the containment then collapsed beneath the weight of the water, which overflowed onto the pad and ground outside of the pad. Ms. Breitenbach estimates that 110 barrels of fluid, some of which was rain water, escaped containment. Elevated conductivity was noted at several spots on and off of the pad, including beneath the containment liner and along the eastern grassy slope that led to the basin. At the time of the inspection, Moody and Associates, Inc. was on site to assess the extent of the release and assist with remediation. Excavation crews were present to begin removal of the contaminated materials.The problem has been contained and there do not appear to be any further threats to the surrounding site.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78a55(i)5vi - EMERGNCY RESPONSE – Planning - Failure of the unconventional well operator to have a copy of the emergency response plan at the well site during all phases of operation.
Violation ID: 971340
Permit API: 129-25570
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Hempfield Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/03/2022
Comments: On October 3, 2022, the Department conducted an inspection on the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. Present were myself and WQS Samuel Steingrabe. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3343707 where violations were outstanding due to deteriorated production fluid tanks that were discharging onto the ground, a missing Act 9 sign and Emergency Response plans. Also, no production reports have been submitted since 2014 per Department database. The following was observed:No Act 9 sign was present at the well site entrance (see photos 2 and 3). No Emergency Response plans, or other required postings were onsite. The production fluid tanks onsite appear to have been replaced since IR 3343707 (see photos 5 and 15). Soil conductivity readings were taken underneath and around these tanks to determine whether petroleum products and/or production fluids were still present in the soil since IR 3343707. These readings were taken underneath the production fluid tank valves and in bare spots in their surrounding earthen berms. An additional reading was taken in a wet spot next to the tank farthest from the site entrance. The reading taken underneath the valve of the tank closest to the site entrance read 100 Micro Siemens (see photo 6). The one taken in the surrounding berm read 111 Micro Siemens (see photo 7). The soil conductivity reading taken underneath the valve of the tank farthest from the site entrance read 380 Micro Siemens (see photo 9). The one taken in a bare spot in the surrounding earthen berm read 640 Micro Siemens (see photo 11). The additional reading taken in the wet spot adjacent to the brine tank read 390 Micro Siemens (see photo 8). A background conductivity reading was taken in a well-vegetated spot at the well site entrance, reading 250 Micro Siemens see photo 16). No well tag was observed on the well or associated equipment with correct information (see photo 13), and the well API number was written on the meter box with sharpie. Additional piping and production equipment was left onsite (see photo 10). Some tire rutting was observed at the back of the well site looking from the road, which could be due to third party traversing (see photo 14). The ground overall was soft, which could lead to future stabilization concerns. Therefore, the Department recommends that the operator take additional stabilization measures to prevent any potential E and S issues from developing. Based on observations from today's inspection, the impacted soil appears to have been removed as of October 3, 2022 and violations against the production fluid tanks have been corrected. However, outstanding violations that were continued in IR 3343707 due to production fluid discharge on the ground shall remain open since no NOV response or any information requested has been received from the operator to evaluate whether the release was remediated in accordance with chapter 78a. All other violations shall remain open as well since the rest of the site remains unchanged since IR 3343707.

Inspection Date: 2019-10-30
Comments: On October 30, 2019 , DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a spill investigation (CTS # 346141) at Alta Operating LLC. COP Tract 285 Pad G. The spill was reported at 0935 that a plug in the dump line of one of the GPUs was not replaced after maintenance on the line was completed. This caused a spill of about 1.9 bbls into the secondary containment and the pad surface. The DEP met with Alta staff Rick Hall and Mark Barbier, they estimated that about a 1 bbl was spilled outside of containment. During the investigation, there was a vacuum tank onsite dewatering the secondary containment of the GPUs. There is a ground wire in the area of the spill, so they were awaiting staff to locate the wire before excavation of the impacted soil could begin. The area of impact is approximately 10'x60'. Water in the secondary containment was screened for conductivity and returned a reading of 1070 uS/cm. A puddle of water in the impacted area was screened and returned a conductivity reading of 5,500 uS/cm. One 25 yard rollback dumpster was onsite to dispose of the impacted soil. The release of production fluid outside of secondary containment is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Section 301 of the Solid Waste Management Act and §78a.54. Due to the volume of the production fluid spilled outside of containment, characterization of the extent of the pollution in accordance of §78a.66(c). The DEP recommends proceeding in accordance with Act 2 remediation.

Due to the volume of the production fluid spilled outside of containment, characterization of the extent of the pollution in accordance of §78a.66(c). The DEP recommends proceeding in accordance with Act 2 remediation.

Comments: On 02/11/2026, an incident inspection was conducted at the Veres Well Pad in Greene Township, Greene County following notification of a spill that occurred on 2/11/2026 from Greylock. I received a call from Trevor Wood, a representative from Greylock notifying me of the spill. I responded to the incident prior to it being assigned to Oil and Gas in our complaint system. I was accompanied by Keith from Greylock onsite. Per Greylock, the spill was reported to the Department's emergency hotline on 02/11/2026. It was reported that 1-3 bbls of produced water from a truck was released onto the pad on 02/11/2026. The spill was identified at 8:50 AM and reported to the hotline at approximately 9:43 AM. No waters of the Commonwealth were impacted.The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. The Emergency Response Plan was onsite at the site entrance (Photo 1).The access road appeared to be in generally good condition and maintained (Photo 2).The spill occurred when a water truck was drawing down produced water from tank. It was believed a pump failed which caused produced water to spray onto the pad, tank and along tank containment. The area impacted was approximately 20ft by 20ft. 1-3 barrels (bbls) were released (Photos 3-6).A conductivity reading was taken in the middle of the impacted area and read 9.09 mS/cm. (Photo 7). Conductivity reading taken in gravel adjacent to separators in front of the tanks was 5.90 mS/cm (Photo 8, 9).I did not observe any spray on the backside of the tanks looking toward the spill area (Photo 10). The area was still in the process of remediation and Greylock was waiting on additional equipment to begin remediation. The spill appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. I recommend following Act 2 guidelines.Due to the release of produced water violations of 78a.54, 78a57(a), SWMA 301, and 91.34(a).

Permit API: 051-23720
Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 4/13/2026
Comments: On 4/13/2026, the Department conducted a routine inspection at the Holchin 2 well plugging site in North Union Township, Fayette County. This inspection was conducted in response to a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well, which was submitted by the operator on 3/16/2026. Tyler Hinkle (Next Level Energy) was on site during this inspection. The following was observed during the inspection:Upon arrival, the Department spoke with Next Level Energy representative Tyler Hinkle, who was on site to make minor repairs to the temporary BMPs installed on site and to remove an excavator from site. Hinkle identified during this inspection evidence of third-party disturbance due to livestock grazing on site. The Department recommends that the operator document any third-party disturbances occurring on site, and take reasonable efforts to stop them and prevent accelerated erosion from occurring on site. Temporary Erosion and sedimentation controls are installed downslope of the access road and well site. No evidence of accelerated erosion was observed on site during this inspection. The site E and S/Restoration plans are available in a mailbox on site. The site appears to be staged for well plugging operations, however no machinery related to well plugging is on site at the time of inspection. The gas well is disconnected from the production equipment. No evidence of a spill, such as staining, was observed on site during this inspection. The API number was not visible anywhere on site. While on site, the Department reviewed the site E and S/Restoration plans. The Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is not installed in the location shown in the E and S plan drawing (photos 4 and 15). Although an overall BMP layout drawing exists, the plans state that E and S controls are to be installed at contractor's discretion. At the time of this inspection, the E and S controls appear to be installed on site in a manner that is preventing accelerated erosion and sedimentation from occurring. The Department recommends that that the operator monitor the site and install additional temporary E and S controls as necessary in order to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to occur. The Department recommends that the site E and S/Restoration plans are kept updated via redlining with the BMP's currently installed on site. Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued for failure to failure to follow the E and S plan.An additional violation shall be issued in IR 4177612 for failure to post the API number on site.

Comments: In an effort to prevent the spread of the COVID-19 virus, the Department has conducted this administrative inspection in response to information provided by Chief. Based on the analytical results for isotopic samples collected by Chief at the above-referenced well on 6/17/2019 and 11/15/2019, methane was detected as follows: 25.13 % Methane detected at the Intermediate (9 5/8¿) x Surface (13 3/8¿) casing annulus on 6/17/2019. 0.37 % Methane detected at the Surface casing (13 3/8¿) x Conductor (20¿) annulus on 11/15/2019. 98.26 % Methane detected at the Production (5 ½") x Intermediate (9 5/8¿) casing annulus on 11/15/2019. Code §78a.73(b), §78a81(a)(2) and (3), and §78a.85(a)(5) have been cited. Please note that because your company provided a self-reported notification, no violation was cited for 25 Pa. Code §78a.86, defective cement, for the other annuli where methane was detected. However, Chief is required to comply with the Department¿s regulations, 25 Pa. Code §78a.86, which provides: ¿In a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing, the operator shall report the defect to the Department within 24 hours of discovery by the operator and shall correct the defect. The operator shall correct the defect or submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. If the defect cannot be corrected or an alternate method is not approved by the Department, the well shall be plugged under § 78a.91 ¿ 78a.98 (related to plugging).¿ Therefore, please provide a written response within 30 days of receipt of this Notice of Violation, as to when and how the above listed violations were or will be corrected, and what steps are being taken to prevent their recurrence.

2020-04-27
Report Details
Operator: Chief Oil & Gas Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-04-27
Violation Code: 78a81(a)3 - CASING AND CEMENTING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Operator conducted casing and cementing activities that failed to prevent pollution or diminution of fresh groundwater.
Violation ID: 883517
Permit API: 015-23430
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Overton Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2020-04-27
Comments: In an effort to prevent the spread of the COVID-19 virus, the Department has conducted this administrative inspection in response to information provided by Chief. Based on the analytical results for isotopic samples collected by Chief at the above-referenced well on 6/17/2019 and 11/15/2019, methane was detected as follows: 25.13 % Methane detected at the Intermediate (9 5/8¿) x Surface (13 3/8¿) casing annulus on 6/17/2019. 0.37 % Methane detected at the Surface casing (13 3/8¿) x Conductor (20¿) annulus on 11/15/2019. 98.26 % Methane detected at the Production (5 ½") x Intermediate (9 5/8¿) casing annulus on 11/15/2019. The presence of methane at the Surface casing (13 3/8¿) x Conductor (20¿) is evidence of defective cement with methane outside of the surface casing string. As a result, violations of 25 Pa. Code §78a.73(b), §78a81(a)(2) and (3), and §78a.85(a)(5) have been cited. Please note that because your company provided a self-reported notification, no violation was cited for 25 Pa. Code §78a.86, defective cement, for the other annuli where methane was detected. However, Chief is required to comply with the Department¿s regulations, 25 Pa. Code §78a.86, which provides: ¿In a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing, the operator shall report the defect to the Department within 24 hours of discovery by the operator and shall correct the defect. The operator shall correct the defect or submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. If the defect cannot be corrected or an alternate method is not approved by the Department, the well shall be plugged under § 78a.91 ¿ 78a.98 (related to plugging).¿ Therefore, please provide a written response within 30 days of receipt of this Notice of Violation, as to when and how the above listed violations were or will be corrected, and what steps are being taken to prevent their recurrence.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to CABOT OIL & GAS CORP in Auburn Twp, Susquehanna County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/19/2021 to CABOT OIL & GAS CORP in Auburn Twp, Susquehanna county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CABOT OIL & GAS CORP
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/20/2017
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 934388
Permit API: 115-22174
Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Auburn Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/19/2021
Comments: On site today in response to a water complaint in the area. This is a FUI (Follow Up Inspection) for the (4) wells on the pad that were inspected on 10/14/21. They are the Howell 2H, 4H, 6H and 8H. All were in production at time of inspection. Remedial work was completed on the 2H, 4H and 6H wells at the end of 2017 to address previous violations cited on the 6H well. - Met w/ lease operator Ben Whitaker to perform isolated gas screenings of the cemented annuli. - All (4) wells have the (20x13) and (13x9) annuli isolated and venting to atmosphere. The (20x13) annuli are plumbed to surface via 3/8" SS tubing, the (13x9) and (9x5) annuli are plumbed to surface w/ 2" pipe. The (9x5) annuli are venting to a shared poly tank w/ an LEL of 100% and CH4 of 5%. Gas was detected in the(20x13) cemented annulus of the 6H and the 8H. Flow checks were performed by lease operator using an ALICAT micro flow meter. No gas flow was detected at any of these wells (20x13) or (13x9) cemented annuli. - The (20x13) and (13x9) annuli of all the wells on the pad were left open and venting to atmosphere upon completion of gas screenings and flow checks. - Individual prod. casing pressures listed below: - 2H: 631 psi., capillary string - 4H: 618 psi., capillary string - 6H: 658 psi., capillary string - 8H: 660 psi. ** Although gas was detected at the (20x13) cemented annuli of the 6H and the 8H wells, no flow was detected via Cabots O&G's ALICAT micro flow meter. This appears to remain indicative of commingling, residual gas within the vent lines and/ or annular spaces. On 9/3/2020 The Dept. requested that Cabot assess these conditions further and contact the Dept. with Cabots assessments. On 6/26/2021 Cabot O&G submitted a "Gas Migration Final Report" including a summary of previous remedial work performed on wells and an assessment of these residual gas detections. - No other violations or obvious concerns were noted.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNFIELD ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/18/2021
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 927036
Permit API: 053-30017
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Harmony Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/18/2021
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to Pennfield Energy's 8/17/2021 notification of a crude oil discharge from a stock tank located at the Milford South tank battery, which is located adjacent to this well site. Per Matt Duckett (field representative for Pennfield Energy) the oil/water separator that serves this tank battery failed and resulted in all production fluids entering the stock tank, which did not have the capacity to hold all of the fluid. Crude oil then discharged from an open vent on top of one of the stock tanks and onto the ground within an earthen containment that surrounds all of the tanks at the Milford South tank battery. The estimated quantity of crude oil that was released has been revised after conducting remediation work. Matt Duckett stated that approximately five barrels of crude is a more accurate quantity of product actually released as a result of this incident. Additional details regarding the release can be found in the 'Remarks/Violations' section of this report. This well is equipped for production with a pump jack, a site ID sign is posted on the jack's electric box.

properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 10/27/2022 to RIYAN FARM & GAS LLC in Allegheny Twp, Cambria county. OGA3211(H) - WELL PERMITS - LABELING - Failure to install, in a permanent manner, the permit number on a completed well.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RIYAN FARM & GAS LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 10/27/2022
Violation Code: OGA3211(H) - WELL PERMITS - LABELING - Failure to install, in a permanent manner, the permit number on a completed well.
Violation ID: 974493
Permit API: 021-20908
Unconventional: No
County: Cambria
Municipality: Allegheny Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/27/2022
Comments: Follow up inspection of the Yahner 1 well conducted on 10/27/2022. Arrived on location at 9:40. Violations were issued during a 3/23/2021 inspection (Inspection Record No. 3166383) for: OGA3211(H) - Failure to install permit number on well. 78.88(A) - Failure to record and retain MIA inspection results. 78.88(b)1-4 - Failure to meet minimum requirements for MIA inspections. 78.121(A) - Failure to submit annual production report. OGA3220(A) - Failure to plug the well upon abandoning it. A follow up inspection was conducted on 3/10/2022 (Inspection Record No. 3327521). This inspection found that none of the previously cited violations had been addressed or responded to and all violations remained outstanding. This 10/26/2022 follow up inspection found that the well remains in a similar condition/configuration as the previous inspections. Well head and tie in line is the only equipment installed. No additional production equipment on location. Appears to have been a new line installed to the well as seen by the adjacent earth disturbance at the time of inspection. There is no API or other identification posted on location. Review found that no Annual Production Reports or Mechanical Integrity Assessment Reports have been submitted. Well is still reported as Inactive Status although the Inactive Status expired on 1/1/2018. Due to failing to return the well to Active status, a violation of 78.104 is issued - terms of Inactive Status. Due to no production of the well reported it is considered abandoned. All previously issued violations remain outstanding.
